findings.title: popover_demolish_hit's positive demolish path (junction gate, button hit, demolish_node/demolish_pipe, the NEW pipe leg) never executes in any scripted scenario — the shared hit-test is pinned for wiring only
findings.location: harness/parity.odin:813-816 (ui_hook wired only for input_parity_esc_ui) + app/input/mouse.odin:145-148 (map-time deselect clears sel before the hook) + app/input/exec.odin:437-475
findings.evidence: parity.odin:813-816: 'ui_hook: proc(rawptr, ^inp.Input, rl.Vector2) -> bool = nil / if sc.name == "input_parity_esc_ui" { ui_hook = parity_ui_press_effect }'; parity.odin:128: 'return inp.popover_demolish_hit(ictx, pos)'; mouse.odin:145-148: 'if esc_deselect { inp.sel_pipe = -1; inp.sel_node = -1 }' — the only hook-wiring scenario clears the selection BEFORE the press branch, so the shared helper always early-returns at sel_node/sel_pipe < 0; exec.odin:452-461 (the new pipe leg) is unreachable in the harness.
findings.detail: The delta moved the demolish-button hit-test into shared code and added a pipe leg, but every scripted press sees sel already cleared — a broken button rect, a drifted junction gate, or wrong pipe-anchor math keeps all 22 scenarios green. App-side mouse behavior is byte-equivalent (read-verified); this is a pin-fidelity gap on the round's new shared code, not a behavior defect.
findings.recommended_fix: Add positive-pin scenarios: select a junction, press the demolish-button center (no ESC), assert Cmd_Demolish_Node + swallow; plus the pipe twin (select pipe, button press, assert Cmd_Demolish_Pipe) to exercise the new leg and pipe_popover_anchor.

findings.title: pipe_popover_anchor duplicates the pipe-midpoint math render already computes inline in draw_demolish_popover
findings.evidence: exec.odin: 'sa, _ := pp.node_slot(t, t.pipe_a[ps]) ... return {(a.x + b.x) / 2, (a.y + b.y) / 2}'; popover.odin:88-92: 'sa, _ := pp.node_slot(topo, topo.pipe_a[ps]) ... anchor := rl.Vector2{(a.x + b.x) / 2, (a.y + b.y) / 2}' — and popover.odin:9-11 declares layout is owned HERE.
findings.detail: The 'ONE copy' claim covers the hit-test copies; the anchor math now lives in input.pipe_popover_anchor AND inline in render, whose header declares it owns the layout — a future anchor change in render silently drifts the input hit-test. Pre-existing in kind (main.odin's pipe_anchor duplicated it before); the delta relocated, not introduced, it.
findings.recommended_fix: Hoist the midpoint into render (e.g. rnd.pipe_popover_anchor(v, topo, ps) next to the rects it owns) and call it from both draw_demolish_popover and input.

findings.title: pipe_popover_anchor discards node_slot's ok — safe only via the caller's pipe_slot guard (implicit invariant)
findings.evidence: 'sa, _ := pp.node_slot(t, t.pipe_a[ps]) / sb, _ := pp.node_slot(t, t.pipe_b[ps])' then node_pos[sa]/node_pos[sb] — the only caller (popover_demolish_hit, exec.odin:455) guards pipe_slot ok first; a live pipe implies live endpoints. Verbatim move of the removed app-side pipe_anchor (same discarded oks) — no behavior drift.
findings.detail: No OOB today; the invariant is implicit and a future caller skipping the pipe_slot guard would read garbage slots.
findings.recommended_fix: Check both node_slot oks and early-return a zero vector on failure (defense in depth), or leave with a comment naming the caller-side guard.
